thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert: prod-east token latency spike + increased 5xx rate. Suspected KV cache growth + continuous-batching backlog. Paging oncall: @elena :rotating_light:
elena: acked. pulling up grafana now. any recent deploys?
matt: I rolled a small model-quantization runtime tweak ~10m ago but that shouldn't touch KV. checking runtime logs.
opsbot: automated rule triggered: kv_cache_memory_usage > 85% in prod-east (cluster: pe-rt-7).
elena: ok first step — throttle continuous batching and raise kv eviction aggressiveness. I'm going to flip the batch throttling FF to canary on 2 workers. @lia i'll handover canary watch to you once it's rolled.
ryan: list of quick mitigations we can do:
- set feature flag `continuous_batching.enabled` -> false for prod-east canary pool
- lower `batching.max_window_ms` to 30ms
- bump `kv.cache_eviction_threshold` from 0.85 -> 0.6 for affected hosts
- per-customer override for big customers to single-request routing

elena: publishing the commands I'm running — watch logs/grafana: :eyes:
```
# throttle continuous batching on host pool pe-rt-7-canary
curl -X POST https://flag-admin.internal/flags/continuous_batching.enabled/toggle \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"scope":"pool:pe-rt-7-canary","value":false}'

# set eviction threshold
curl -X POST https://config-api.internal/clusters/pe-rt-7/config \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"kv.cache_eviction_threshold":0.6}'
```

matt: logs show a ton of prefix keys pinned. sample from runtime errors (stdout tail):
```
2026-03-15T02:08:12Z [warning] kv_cache: growth detected, pinned_entries=123456, evict_candidate_scan_ms=1200
2026-03-15T02:08:14Z [error] batching: backlog length 4300, avg_latency_ms=210
2026-03-15T02:08:15Z [error] serve: OOM avoidance kicking in, rejecting new requests
```

lia: can confirm canary command succeeded on 2 nodes (pe-rt-7-canary-01, -02). continuous_batching toggled off. also applied eviction threshold. watching telemetry now. linking grafana panels: https://grafana.internal/d/kv/kv-cache-overview?orgId=1&var-cluster=pe-rt-7

elena: good. next: apply per-customer override for "AcmeCorp" — their traffic is dominating the batch shapes. We'll route them to dedicated single-request pipeline until we stabilize. ryan can you prepare the override?
ryan: on it. command: 
```
curl -X POST https://routing.internal/overrides \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"customer_id":"acme-123","route":"single_request","duration_minutes":60}'
```

ryan: override applied. Acme traffic now on single-request path (confirmed via access logs).

matt: metrics: 5xx rate dropping from 4.8% -> 1.3% on canary nodes. token latency p95 from 420ms -> 110ms on canary. cluster-wide still elevated because full rollout not yet.

elena: start controlled rollout. policy: 2 nodes -> 8 nodes -> full cluster. pause 3m between steps, rollback on any >1% increase in 5xx or p95 > 300ms. I'll run the canary->8 nodes rollout now.

opsbot: rollout job started: flag-change continuous_batching.enabled -> false (scope: pe-rt-7, targets: 8 nodes). job_id=RJ-6621

lia: monitoring watch handoff: I'm taking 30m active watch from elena after this step. @matt you'll stay on runtime logs. @ryan watch routing/overrides.

elena: noted. handing off to @lia in 5. leaving a quick checklist in thread.

lia: confirm: canary metrics holding. performing second step to 8 nodes.

matt: seeing a small regression on nodes with older kernels — p95 spikes to ~260ms for a minute after toggle, then recovers. triggers ok so far.

elena: continue. if we see sustained p95 > 300ms escalate to rollback. opsbot will auto-rollback if 5xx > 2% for more than 90s.

incident-bot: NOTE: customer-impact classification updated -> "partial degradation" for realtime gen endpoints in region prod-east. Affected customers: acme-123 (mitigated), beta-inc (minor).

customer-support: pinging here — CS notified acme about temporary throttling path and provided mitigation ETA.

lia: after 3rd step (full cluster) metrics stabilized: cluster 5xx down to 0.8%, p95 token latency 125ms. CPU/GPU utilization normalizing. KV cache memory usage dropping from 92% -> 58% over 8 minutes.

ryan: removed per-customer override for acme (they're back on normal path).
matt: logs show fewer pinned prefixes, eviction throughput increased.

elena: marking immediate mitigation as successful. next: schedule postmortem, assign cleanup tasks and add automated guard to alert earlier next time.

lia: summary notes for postmortem (copying to thread):
- trigger: sudden KV cache blowup related to long-lived pinned prefix keys + continuous batching inflating batches -> backlog.
- immediate mitigations: toggle continuous_batching off (canary->gradual rollout), lower kv eviction threshold, per-customer routing override for top noisy customers.
- customer impact: partial degradation for prod-east gen endpoints, Acme had outages for ~6 minutes before override; now resolved.
- metrics: peak 5xx 5.1% at 02:09 -> 0.8% after full rollout. KV memory 92%->58% in 10 minutes.
- owner for postmortem: @matt (eng-runtime), due EOD local.
- follow-ups: add `pinned_prefix_scan` alert, add preemptive throttle when kv_cache growth rate > X keys/min, hard cap per-customer batch size.

matt: I'll draft the postmortem and open follow-up tickets. assigning `ENG-4523` to runtime to hard-cap batch growth and `ENG-4524` to infra for better guardrails.

elena: huge thanks everyone. main oncall handoff reminder: @lia you'll carry active watch for next 30m then hand to next rotation at 03:00 UTC.

lia: acknowledged. leaving final note: no immediate rollback required, no hotfix deploy to binaries needed — feature-flag + config changes solved the issue. will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident P1 resolved -> mitigation in place, monitoring continues. Postmortem assigned to matt.

lia: closing active incident channel after 30m monitoring window. if anything flares, ping this thread.
